chosen.premise: If Exeggutor’s three heads choose different directions, their conflicting wills make the whole Pokémon unable to move.
chosen.hook: Three minds can make Exeggutor completely freeze.
chosen.visualIdea: Put arrows over the three heads pointing different ways as Exeggutor’s body locks in place.
chosen.note: A highly distinctive behavioral rule with direct Pokédex support and an immediately readable visual conflict.

candidates.visualIdea: Put arrows over the three heads pointing different ways as Exeggutor’s body locks in place.

candidates.premise: When one of Exeggutor’s heads drops off, it continues life as an Exeggcute cluster.
candidates.hook: Exeggutor can literally lose a head—and create its pre-evolution.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Exeggutor shedding one head, which transitions into a cluster of Exeggcute.
candidates.note: Exceptionally specific and bizarre; the Pokédex supports the head becoming Exeggcute, though the wording is framed as something that is said to happen rather than a guaranteed life cycle.

candidates.premise: Strong sunlight makes Exeggutor’s heads grow larger until an oversized head can fall off and become Exeggcute.
candidates.hook: For Exeggutor, too much sunlight can make its head fall off.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate the heads swelling under bright sunlight, then one popping off and becoming Exeggcute.
candidates.note: Strong visual escalation, but it combines separate entries and slightly overstates the causal chain by implying that sunlight directly makes a head fall off.

candidates.premise: Alolan Exeggutor changes from 2 meters and 120 kilograms to 10.9 meters and 415.6 kilograms—and gains Dragon typing.
candidates.hook: Exeggutor has a regional form that is over five times taller.
candidates.visualIdea: Place standard and Alolan Exeggutor side by side with height, weight, and type changes animated on screen.
candidates.note: Excellent numerical comparison with strong visual proof; the regional-form transformation is familiar to many fans, reducing surprise slightly.

candidates.premise: Exeggutor’s three heads each fire psychokinetic energy, tripling its psychic power when they attack together.
candidates.hook: Exeggutor’s secret weapon is three psychic attacks at once.
candidates.visualIdea: Three separate psychic beams merge into one oversized blast labeled “tripled power.”
candidates.note: Clear and well supported, but the psychic-power premise is less inherently surprising than Exeggutor’s head-shedding biology.

candidates.premise: Exeggutor’s heads think independently and can be noisy, yet they use telepathy to reach joint decisions without squabbling.
candidates.hook: Three independent minds somehow run one friendly Pokémon.
candidates.visualIdea: Give each head a different thought bubble, then connect all three with telepathic lines to one decision.
candidates.note: Supported by several entries and contains a fun contradiction, but it is more of a personality profile than one sharply defined rule.

rounds.request: None needed; the chosen angle is strong. A stronger alternative would need an equally strange, Pokémon-specific biological rule with direct Pokédex support and a clear transformation or on-screen payoff.
